summary: Engadget previews Apple's "Scary Fast" event on October 30, 2023, an unusual 8PM ET evening presentation. Rumors from Ming-Chi Kuo and Mark Gurman point to M3-series chips, new MacBook Pro models, a refreshed 24-inch iMac and USB-C versions of Apple's Magic accessories, with a possible iPad Pro update less certain. The article also notes supply constraints and sales context behind the timing.
one_line: Engadget previews Apple's Scary Fast event, expecting M3 chips, M3 MacBook Pros, a new 24-inch iMac and USB-C Magic accessories.
key_facts: Apple's "Scary Fast" event is on October 30, the night before Halloween, and starts at 8PM ET, an unusual evening slot.
It has been nearly 17 months since the M2 SoC debuted; the M2 series debuted 19 months after the M1.
Ming-Chi Kuo suggested "M3 series MacBook Pro" will be the event's focus, implying more than one new SoC such as an M3 Pro and maybe an M3 Max.
Mark Gurman of Bloomberg reported a new 24-inch iMac is expected this month and that the iMac is in short supply at Apple retail stores.
The most recent 24-inch iMac was an M1 model that arrived in April 2021.
Gurman noted the 13-inch, 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro all have extended shipping times on Apple's web store, and said Apple has been testing M3 Max and M3 Pro MacBook Pro models.
Kuo previously cited limited supply of between 400,000 and 500,000 M3 laptop units and said supply may stay tight until early 2024.
Kuo said MacBook sales waned this year mainly due to "the limited M2 computing power upgrade."
If M3 models don't boost sales, Kuo suggests a MacBook Pro with a new design is more likely in 2025, and Apple may add a cheaper MacBook with an annual sales target of 8 million to 10 million.
Gurman suggests USB-C versions of the Magic Trackpad, Magic Mouse and Magic Keyboard will appear, following the iPhone 15's switch from Lightning and a USB-C Apple Pencil.
The USB-C shift was prompted by European Union rules requiring a standard charging port on certain devices.
Engadget has a hunch an iPad Pro will appear despite Gurman's doubts; the latest iPad Pro debuted a year ago with the M2 replacing the M1.
